newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Havel does not need severe cancer therapies - agency.
newsitem.headline: Havel does not need severe cancer therapies - agency.

text.p: Czech President Vaclav Havel, recovering from surgery to remove a malignant tumour from his lung last month, does not require chemical or radiation treatment, CTK news agency reported.
It quoted a deputy health minister as saying Havel's recovery from the operation which removed half of the right lobe of his lung on December 2 was satisfactory.
A council of Czech and international specialists had concluded that only normal post-operative treatment would be necessary, it said.
Havel, 60, the dissident playwright who led Prague's 1989 bloodless revolution over communism, entered hospital in late December with what his office said was pneumonia.
Exploratory surgery revealed a small cancerous tumour and doctors immediately decided on radical surgery in the hope of removing all of the cancerous cells at an early stage.

Havel, a chain smoker for most of his life, was released from hospital the day after Christmas and has been recovering in his private villa in western Prague, able to perform a few official functions.
